payload.comment_body:
## Build Update

The committed delivery adds matching repository-root `Makefile` and `make.cmd` adapters for `worktree`, `typecheck`, `test`, `build`, and fail-fast `quality`; routes the Pages build job through `make quality`; and documents both platform entry points in README. The worktree setup validates `FAKTORIAL_WORKTREE_PATH`, quotes paths, and installs the lockfile with `npm ci`.

The investigation baseline passed `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (69 files passed, 7 skipped; 701 tests passed, 16 skipped), and `npm run build`. On the assigned clean head `b8cfaf70330b3d06c6d279a1ae05f91e653ce0c5`, allowed static checks passed again: `make -n quality` expanded typecheck, test, and build in order; missing `FAKTORIAL_WORKTREE_PATH` and an unsupported Windows target each returned exit code 2 with actionable guidance; and `git diff --check main...HEAD` returned 0. No task-specific durable proof obligations were declared. Full adapter execution remains intentionally assigned to Faktorial's canonical verifier.

No UI areas, generated assets, screenshots, ADRs, or runtime notes are required. The committed task delta contains only `.github/workflows/pages.yml`, `Makefile`, `make.cmd`, and `README.md`; runtime result artifacts are absent from Git.

pull_request_description.delivered_outcome: A repository-owned, cross-platform build and test contract now prepares Faktorial worktrees and runs the complete typecheck, Vitest, and production-build gate consistently for contributors and Pages CI.
pull_request_description.implementation_approach: Added aligned GNU Make and Windows batch adapters with direct worktree, typecheck, test, build, and fail-fast quality targets. Worktree setup validates and quotes the supplied checkout path before running `npm ci`; Pages CI now calls the canonical quality target, and README documents both platforms.
pull_request_description.solution_rationale: Thin adapters preserve the existing npm scripts as the source of build behavior while giving Faktorial and CI stable native entry points. Sequential target invocation keeps failures visible and avoids introducing another build framework or changing application behavior.
pull_request_description.tradeoffs_and_alternatives: The adapters intentionally delegate to existing npm scripts, so there is minor platform-specific wrapper duplication but no dependency or script migration risk. A Node-based orchestration script could reduce wrapper duplication, but would add an unnecessary layer and weaken native Make/Windows discovery. Optional simulation and optimization commands remain outside the canonical quality gate.
pull_request_description.architectural_decisions:
The repository verification process now has one canonical quality boundary used by local adapters and Pages CI; deployment permissions, artifact upload, and deploy ordering remain unchanged.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  F[Faktorial or contributor] --> Q[Repository quality adapter]
  C[Pages CI] --> Q
  Q --> T[TypeScript check]
  T --> V[Vitest suite]
  V --> B[Vite production build]
```
pull_request_description.verification: The investigation clean-head baseline passed dependency installation, typecheck, 69 active test files with 701 passing tests, and the three-entry Vite build. Static re-entry checks confirmed GNU Make command order, Windows missing-path and unknown-target exit code 2 behavior, a clean task diff, and no committed runtime artifacts. Canonical `run-quality` verification is requested and pending.
